chapter_theme: The last seven herding songs leave the cattle behind and tell the herdsman what to see: the lotus in the head, the Real sought in the sky with true knowledge, the mirror that only the eye of knowledge can see, the void that only the subtle intellect can point to, the eternal that stands forever, Shakti and the Supreme blended within oneself in nishta, and, like an owl, silence, by which the kindled round of birth is cut.
structure_note: 1857 to 1863 complete the கிடை கட்டுதல் of chapter 95 and the whole work. The herding image survives only in the address கோனே; each stanza is a two-line instruction on seeing (தெரிந்து, காண், கண்டு), ending in silence and the cutting of birth.

1857.reading: Know the sight of the lotus in the head, our herdsman; and know in your mind the technique by which the mouth attains its power.
1857.nuance: சிரமதில் கமலம் is the lotus at the crown, the highest of the supports in the yogic body; சேவை is service or, as here, the sight of a deity. வாய் சித்திக்கும் தந்திரம் is unclear: the method by which speech gains power (வாக்குசித்தி), or the mouth's part in drawing the nectar of the milking songs; tradition takes it as the former.

1858.reading: Seeking the sky, see the Real in true knowledge, herdsman; always holding truth in truth, go on in true knowledge.
1858.nuance: வத்து is வஸ்து, the Real; மெய்யே மெய்யில் கொண்டு piles the word for truth three times in a line. விண் நாடி is 'seeking the sky', though a coded ear hears விண்நாடி, the sky-channel, that is the central channel; the plain reading stands on its own.

1859.reading: Look and see inside the mirror, herdsman; without the eye of knowledge the mirror cannot be seen, our herdsman.
1859.nuance: The mirror is the mind or the inner faculty in which the Real is reflected, as in Tirumular's magic mirror of the mind; the twist is that the mirror itself is invisible to the ordinary eye, so ஞானக்கண், the eye of knowledge, is needed before any reflection can be sought. கண்ணடி is a shortened கண்ணாடி.

1860.reading: Where are those who can point to the void, herdsman? Hold the thought that only the subtle intellect can point it out.
1860.nuance: சூனியம், the void, is the Siddhars' word for the nothing that is the goal; சுட்டுவார், those who can point, denies that it can be shown from outside, and புத்தி சூக்குமம், the subtle intellect, is the one faculty allowed to reach it. The claim is that the void is known, not that it is unknowable.

1861.reading: If the eternal comes straight to you, that is the state, herdsman; see that it stands forever and see it with certainty, our herdsman.
1861.nuance: நித்தியம் is the eternal, set against the perishing world of 1815; நேர்படில், if it comes straight or meets one, suggests a meeting rather than an effort. நிச்சயம் காண், see with certainty, makes settled conviction part of the seeing. The syntax of line 1 is compressed.

1862.reading: Shakti and the Supreme are blended within you, herdsman; if you achieve nishta, both can be seen within you.
1862.nuance: The gloss gives நிட்டை as Sivayoga, the fixed absorption; the verse makes the union of Shakti and Param an inner fact first and a thing seen second, so nishta reveals rather than produces it. The body as the place of the divine pair is the Siddhars' body-as-cosmos claim in its devotional form.

1863.reading: Stay like an owl and achieve silence, our herdsman; see the supreme root-state and cut off the kindled round of birth.
1863.nuance: The owl is still and silent by day and awake in the dark, so it is the figure for the sage's silence here, where in Pattinathar it is the figure for blindness to the light; the same bird carries opposite senses. பர மூலநிலை, the supreme root-state, is the source itself; மூட்டுப் பிறப்பு, birth kindled like a fire, is the round that silence puts out. The work ends on this cutting of birth.

links.note: Tirumular says a magic mirror has risen in the mind, yet people do not see even its reflection and will not polish it; Idaikkadar says that without the eye of knowledge the mirror itself cannot be seen. Both make the inner mirror something present but unseen, and both blame the faculty of the viewer rather than the mirror.

Pattiragiriyar asks when he will see and know as light within a mirror instead of measuring distances; Idaikkadar says the mirror can be seen only with the eye of knowledge. Both make the mirror the figure for immediate inner seeing, and Idaikkadar adds the condition Pattiragiriyar leaves implicit.

Tirumular says the Lady of the tattvas makes her way through the flesh and dwells within us, and the body becomes Siva's temple; Idaikkadar says Shakti and the Supreme are blended within oneself and are seen there in nishta. Both locate the divine pair in the body; Tirumular has her come in by grace, Idaikkadar has her already there to be seen.

Both use the owl. In Pattinathar the sun is darkness to the owl's eye, so the owl is the unknowing man blind to a light that is present; in Idaikkadar the herdsman is told to stay like an owl and reach silence, so the owl is the still, night-waking sage. The same bird is the figure for blindness in one and for watchful silence in the other.

Tirumular says silence is when speech and mind are both still, and that silence of the tongue alone is mere muteness; Idaikkadar tells the herdsman to be like an owl, achieve silence, and so cut off birth. The owl's stillness is of the whole creature, which fits Tirumular's demand that mind as well as speech be quiet.

new_concepts.gloss: the void: the nothing that cannot be pointed at or shown, which the Siddhars name as the Real and say only the subtle intellect can reach
new_concepts.label_source: verses use the word (1860 சூனியமானத்தைச் சுட்டுவார் எங்குண்டு); the id follows chapter 102, which adds the same concept

source_issues: Chapter 96 holds only seven verses because the work ends at seq 1863; the chapter break falls inside the கிடை கட்டுதல் section, which runs from 1846.
1859 line 2 prints கண்ணடி for கண்ணாடி, a shortening or slip; the sense is unaffected.
